Although KinForge is still built in Unreal Engine, developments like this could give companies that create game engines cause for concern. titulo: Redict deprecated in favor of Valkey
resumo: Drew DeVault has announced that Redict , a fork of Redis that was created in response to Redis's 2024 license change , has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey , the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file. I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community. We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey, which uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when Redis has a bad financial quarter.

titulo: Proton launches a privacy-first AI assistant for your PC
resumo: Proton has released its AI assistant as a standalone computer app, Lumo Desktop. The app can search for documents on your computer and retrieve information from connected services such as Google Drive and Proton Mail. Through Connections, the assistant can also work with local folders, run commands, and retrieve content from the web. Users decide for themselves which actions Lumo is allowed to perform automatically, which require approval, and which should be blocked entirely. Proton Another new feature is called Schedules, which lets you automate recurring tasks such as compiling emails every week or regularly reviewing documents and other information. Proton has also introduced Skills, reusable instructions that control how the assistant carries out specific tasks. According to the company, neither conversations nor information from connected apps is used to train AI models. Chat history is also protected by encryption designed to prevent even Proton itself from reading the content. Lumo Desktop is available to download for Windows, Linux, and macOS. The program requires a Proton account.

titulo: MIT discovers that aging weakens the brain’s nighttime cleaning system
resumo: MIT researchers have discovered that the brain’s natural waste-removal system becomes significantly less effective during sleep as people age. The decline is linked to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and changes in blood flow, potentially offering new clues about why aging increases the risk of Alzheimer's disease and dementia. Surprisingly, some older adults retain the same powerful cleansing waves seen in younger people.

titulo: Dual-targeted CAR T-cell therapy shows promise in patients with treatment-resistant multiple myeloma
resumo: A first-in-human study by Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute investigators found that a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy called TriPRIL reduced or eliminated signs of cancer in 12 of 15 patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. TriPRIL—short for trimeric APRIL (a proliferation-inducing ligand)—recognizes two proteins on myeloma cells instead of just one. Researchers published their findings in The Lancet.

titulo: These Engineers Are Cleaning Up Connected Cars’ Security Flaws
resumo: Today’s connected vehicles collect and transmit far more personal data from drivers and passengers than their predecessors, with costly consequences. The Center for Automotive Management in Germany estimates that cyberattacks have caused more than $20 billion in damage to the auto industry as of 2025, twenty times higher than in 2022. This week, engineers and cybersecurity researchers are gathering in Bonn, Germany, for the Embedded Security in Cars (escar) conference to discuss using AI for defense, hardening chips, and otherwise securing the auto industry’s data handling. titulo: New approach aims to make treatment more accessible for children with rare brain disorders
resumo: McGill University researchers have developed and tested a new way to facilitate the creation of personalized genetic therapies for children with rare neurodevelopmental disorders. Currently, many children suffering from rare disorders are left without a realistic path to treatment, given that the underlying genetic changes may affect only a handful of patients. As such, there is a need for platforms that treat diagnosis as the starting point for therapeutic evaluation rather than the endpoint of a diagnostic journey.
